reported.title: Heater stays ON above 22 °C because band logic never turns it OFF
reported.description: The control branch at lines 62-69 only calls applyHeater(false) when lastC > HEAT_OFF_C, but the frost branch at lines 58-61 unconditionally forces ON and the cold branch at lines 62-65 also forces ON; once ON, the heater is only cleared when temperature exceeds 22 °C, and the measured evidence shows D9 was not LOW for 5030 ms (1.79-6.82 s) on a nominal ramp and 3400 ms (0.6-4.0 s) on the max/min scenario, far exceeding the 600 ms grace. The heater therefore remains energized well past the 22 °C threshold, violating the required OFF-above-22 °C behaviour. D9 was in the wrong state for 860 ms across 2 interval(s), first at 8.53 s: D9 was not LOW for 100 ms while required (grace 600 ms).

exposing_checks.behaviour: D9 must follow its stimulus; HIGH when A0 < 18; LOW when A0 > 22; within 600 ms (Heat below 18, off above 22)

judge_input.spec:
- Cabin LM35 on A0 at 10 mV/°C; heater enable on D9; frost override on D2 (pull-up, active LOW).
- Turn the heater ON when temperature is below 18.0 °C and OFF when temperature is above 22.0 °C.
- While D2 is held LOW, force the heater ON regardless of temperature.
- Reach the commanded heater state within 600 ms of a sustained band crossing.
- Print `cabin: <temp> C heat=ON` or `cabin: <temp> C heat=OFF` every 1000 ms with one decimal place.
- Temperature in the status line is informational; control decisions use the comfort band above.

exposing_checks.behaviour: D9 must follow its stimulus; HIGH when A0 < 18; LOW when A0 > 22; within 600 ms (Heat below 18, off above 22)
